adjudications.reason: The plan's essential beat requires Julius to mention the Embassy invitation as the alternative to marriage. In the revision, the invitation runs straight into the proposal with no contrast marker, so the logic of the offer blurs. Restoring the source's eight-word pivot repairs this at minimal cost.

evidence.quote: “You think I mind saying it, but I don’t in the least! _Ours_, so there!”
“I owe you something for the relentless way you’ve squashed me whenever I’ve tried to be sentimental.”

adjudications.reason: The payback reading survives without the cut sentence. Tommy prods with 'Whose flat?' and Tuppence answers 'You think I mind saying it', which shows he is pressing her. 'I owe you something for the relentless way you’ve squashed me' cannot be read as plain gratitude, because no one thanks someone for squashing them, so the irony is intact. Restoring the line would cost words against a tight cut target.

The chapter will remain about 58 words over the 600 target rather than lose meaning.
